claims.text: Comedy and philosophy are the only two truth-telling content categories because they deliver context on life through either laughter or reflection.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: When evaluating comedians to follow, consistency of output (regular comedy releases) matters more than follower count; one comedy video among non-comedy posts disqualifies a creator.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Regular output signals commitment to craft and audience respect; irregular output suggests lack of serious practice.
bounded_by: Does not address quality or engagement metrics, only output consistency

claims.text: Live comedy shows are substantially weaker than comedy podcasts because rehearsed sets must be funny identically each performance, whereas podcast conversations gain humor from contextual relevance and prior conversational setup.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Podcast comedy leverages conversational context and audience warmth from prior banter, allowing natural funny moments; live sets require scripted consistency, removing spontaneity.
bounded_by: Observation stated as preference, not universal rule

claims.text: The only content Alex Hormozi does not enjoy is lazy or crude comedy without purpose; specifically crude-for-crude's-sake comedy.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Purpose-driven comedy, even if crude, has intellectual or emotional grounding; purposeless crudeness demonstrates lack of craft.
bounded_by: Personal taste boundary, not claimed as universal principle

examples.text: Alex Hormozi personally follows comedians Andrew Schultz, Whitney Cummings, Sam Morrill, Mark Normand, Nima Nas, Matt Rief, Bill Burr, Nate Bargatzi, and others based on seeing regular comedy output on his newsfeed. When reviewing a creator's profile, if he observes only one comedy video among multiple non-comedy posts, he will not follow them; but if they make regular comedy clips, he will follow them almost regardless of follower count.

Alex Hormozi prefers podcast comedy (Tom Segura, Bert Chrysler, Big Jay Oakerson) to live shows, citing the candid conversational humor and moment-specific jokes as superior to rehearsed material that must land identically with every cold audience. He does not listen to comedy podcasts despite this preference; he watches routines and clips instead.

Alex Hormozi consumes philosophy exclusively from classical/ancient sources (Epictetus, Seneca, Stoics, Dostoevsky). His criterion is biographical finality: 'If you're dead, I like you. That's the way that you get validity for Alex.' He does not follow contemporary philosophy voices.

practices.text: Follow comedians who release comedy clips regularly, regardless of follower count; unfollow accounts with sporadic comedy output mixed with non-comedy content.
Consume philosophy from vetted classical/ancient sources rather than contemporary voices.
Use X (formerly Twitter) as the primary social platform; manage your own tweets without delegation.
